title: Health and illness
about: Collocations for talking about health: catching and developing illnesses, getting injured, keeping fit, and describing pain and treatment, such as catch a cold, vigorous exercise and be taken ill.

parts.title: Verb collocations referring to illnesses and injuries
Common mistakes
parts.note: Про речі кажуть damaged (пошкоджений), про людей — injured або hurt (травмований): The van was badly damaged, but the driver wasn't injured. Рука — це arm (від плеча до кисті) або hand (кисть), а з частинами тіла англійською ставлять my/your: I broke my arm. У таблиці — ще кілька пасток, коли говориш про здоров'я.

items.pattern: catch a cold / (the) flu / a chill / pneumonia · catch – caught – caught
items.meaning: become ill with an infection, often after getting cold or wet or being near someone who is ill
items.example: Put a hat on, or you'll **catch a cold**.
more: My little brother **caught the flu** at nursery, and soon the whole family had it.
Grandad **caught pneumonia** last winter and spent a week in hospital.
items.watchOut: «Застудитися» — catch a cold (або get a cold), а не get cold: get cold — просто замерзнути. «Захворіти на грип» — природно catch/get (the) flu, а не get ill on flu (на — не on). Pneumonia читається без p: /njuːˈməʊniə/.

items.pattern: contract a disease / malaria / typhoid · formal
items.meaning: become ill with a serious disease that you get from people, animals, insects or dirty water; used in formal or written English
items.uk: заразитися (малярією, тифом), захворіти на інфекційну хворобу
items.example: Two members of the expedition **contracted malaria** in the rainforest.
more: She **contracted typhoid** from dirty drinking water while travelling.
Nobody knows exactly how he **contracted the disease**.
items.watchOut: Contract тут — не «укласти контракт», а «заразитися». Це формальне слово для новин і документів; у розмові кажуть get або catch. Про звичайну застуду contract не кажуть.

items.pattern: develop cancer / diabetes / arthritis / Alzheimer's disease · formal
items.meaning: slowly start to have a serious long-term illness
items.example: My aunt **developed diabetes** in her fifties and had to change the way she ate.
more: Smokers are far more likely to **develop lung cancer**.
After years of carrying heavy boxes, he **developed arthritis** in both knees.
items.watchOut: «У неї розвинувся діабет» — англійською підмет людина: she developed diabetes. Catch про такі хвороби не кажуть: діабет чи рак не «ловлять», ними не заражаються.

items.pattern: suffer from asthma / hay fever / backache / migraines
items.meaning: have an illness or health problem, often for a long time or again and again
items.example: My sister **suffers from hay fever**, so May and June are hard for her.
more: Lots of people who sit at a desk all day **suffer from backache**.
Our son **suffers from asthma**, so he never goes anywhere without his inhaler.
items.watchOut: «Страждає на астму» — suffers from asthma, не suffers on asthma. Hay fever — не гарячка, а алергія на пилок: нежить, чхання, сльози.

items.phrase: have an attack of asthma / hay fever
items.pattern: have an attack of asthma / hay fever / bronchitis / diarrhoea · also an asthma attack
items.meaning: suddenly have a short, often bad period of an illness
items.uk: напад (астми, алергії); у когось стався напад
items.example: Grandma **had a bad attack of bronchitis** last winter and couldn't leave the house for a fortnight.
more: Two kids on the school trip **had an attack of diarrhoea**, so a teacher stayed at the hotel with them.
If you **have an attack of asthma**, sit up straight and use your inhaler.
items.watchOut: Напад хвороби — an attack of…, не an assault (assault — напад на людину, злочин). Британське написання — diarrhoea /ˌdaɪəˈrɪə/, американське — diarrhea.

items.pattern: be diagnosed with cancer / diabetes / autism · a diagnosis
items.meaning: be told by a doctor that you have a particular illness or condition
items.example: My neighbour **was diagnosed with diabetes** after a routine blood test.
more: Their son **was diagnosed with autism** when he was three.
If it's **diagnosed** early, this kind of cancer can usually be treated.
items.watchOut: «У нього діагностували рак» — he was diagnosed with cancer: людина — підмет, прийменник with. Не they diagnosed him cancer і не he was diagnosed on cancer.

items.pattern: suffer / sustain (serious / minor / head) injuries · sustain is formal
items.meaning: be hurt in an accident, a fall or a fight
items.example: Three walkers **sustained injuries** when part of the cliff path collapsed.
more: Both riders **suffered injuries** when their horses fell at the same fence.
She **sustained a serious knee injury** while skiing and missed the rest of the season.
items.watchOut: «Отримав травми» — suffered/sustained injuries, не obtained/gained injuries. У розмові простіше: he was injured / he got hurt. Trauma — переважно психологічна травма, а не зламана нога.

items.pattern: a minor / serious / major / head injury
items.meaning: how bad an injury is: minor means small and not dangerous; serious or major means bad and dangerous
items.example: It was only a **minor injury**: two stitches in my chin and a plaster.
more: The climber was flown to hospital with **serious head injuries**.
Most people come back from a ski holiday with nothing worse than **minor injuries** and a few bruises.
items.watchOut: «Легка травма» — a minor injury, не a light/easy injury. «Тяжка травма» — a serious/major injury, не a heavy injury.

items.pattern: take (regular / more) exercise · also do / get exercise
items.meaning: do physical activity to keep your body healthy
items.example: My doctor told me to **take more exercise** and cut down on salt.
more: You don't need a gym to **take exercise**: walking the dog counts too.
I sleep much better when I **take regular exercise**.
items.watchOut: Не make exercise і не make sport. Exercise у цьому значенні незлічуване: more exercise, не more exercises (exercises — окремі вправи, наприклад у підручнику чи в залі).

items.pattern: vigorous / regular / gentle exercise
items.meaning: hard physical activity that makes you breathe fast and sweat
items.example: Twenty minutes of **vigorous exercise**, like running or fast swimming, does you more good than an hour of strolling.
more: Avoid **vigorous exercise** for a week after the operation.
Wait at least an hour after a big meal before you do any **vigorous exercise**.
items.watchOut: «Інтенсивні навантаження» — vigorous exercise, не strong exercise і не powerful exercise. Наголос на перший склад: VIG-or-ous.

items.pattern: eat / have a balanced diet
items.meaning: eat the right mix of different kinds of food
items.example: If you **eat a balanced diet**, you probably don't need vitamin pills.
more: Athletes need **a balanced diet**, not just lots of pasta.
Since I started cooking at home, I've been **eating a more balanced diet**.
items.watchOut: Diet — не лише «дієта для схуднення», а й те, що людина зазвичай їсть: a balanced diet — збалансоване харчування. «Сидіти на дієті» — be on a diet.

items.pattern: healthy eating · a healthy diet / lifestyle
items.meaning: choosing and eating food that is good for your body
items.example: Our local library has a whole shelf of cookbooks about **healthy eating**.
more: **Healthy eating** doesn't have to be expensive: beans, lentils and frozen vegetables are cheap.
The school sends parents a leaflet on **healthy eating** at the start of every year.
items.watchOut: «Здорове (правильне) харчування» — healthy eating або a healthy diet, не right/correct eating і не healthy feeding: feeding — про тварин і немовлят.

items.pattern: follow / start / stick to a fitness programme
items.meaning: do a planned set of exercises regularly over weeks or months
items.example: I've been **following a fitness programme** from a magazine, and now I can run five kilometres.
more: The physio gave me a simple **fitness programme** for my bad back.
If you have heart problems, ask your doctor which **fitness programme** is safe to **follow**.
items.watchOut: Британське написання — programme, американське — program. «Займатися за програмою» — follow a programme, не observe чи fulfil a programme.

items.pattern: stick to a programme / a diet / a plan · stick – stuck – stuck
items.meaning: keep doing what you planned and not give up
items.example: Starting a diet is easy. **Sticking to it** is the hard part.
more: I made a training plan in January but only **stuck to it** for three weeks.
If you **stick to your programme**, you'll see results in a month.
items.watchOut: «Дотримуватися дієти» — stick to a diet (або keep to a diet), не hold a diet і не keep a diet. Прийменник to обов'язковий: stick to it. Минулий час — stuck, не sticked.

items.pattern: keep fit · stay fit · a keep-fit class
items.meaning: stay healthy and strong by doing regular exercise
items.example: My grandparents go swimming twice a week to **keep fit**.
more: How do you **keep fit** when you work such long hours?
Mum goes to a **keep-fit** class at the community centre every Tuesday.
items.watchOut: «Підтримувати форму» — keep fit або stay in shape, не support form і не save form.

items.pattern: be in good / great / bad / terrible shape · get in shape
items.meaning: be fit and healthy (or, with bad or terrible, not fit at all)
items.example: My uncle is seventy, but he's **in really good shape**: he still plays tennis every weekend.
more: I was **in terrible shape** after the winter, so I started cycling to work.
You need to **be in good shape** to walk the whole coast path.
items.watchOut: «У гарній формі» — in good shape, з прийменником in. Figure — це фігура, зовнішній вигляд, а не фізична форма: she has a good figure.

items.pattern: be terminally ill · terminal cancer / illness
items.meaning: having an illness that cannot be cured and will cause death, usually soon
items.example: The hospice looks after **terminally ill** patients and their families.
more: When her father was **terminally ill**, she moved back home to care for him.
He has **terminal cancer**, so the doctors are focusing on keeping him comfortable.
items.watchOut: Terminally не має нічого спільного з «терміново» (urgently): це про хворобу, яку не вилікувати. «Тяжко хворий» — seriously ill, не heavily ill.

items.pattern: be in / suffer excruciating / unbearable pain
items.meaning: pain so bad that it is almost too much to bear
items.example: When I broke my leg, I was in **excruciating pain** until the ambulance arrived.
more: She was in **unbearable pain** for days before the doctors found the cause.
Gallstones can cause **excruciating pain**, so don't ignore the symptoms.
items.watchOut: «Сильний біль» — severe/terrible/excruciating pain, не strong pain і не big pain. «Мені дуже боляче» — I'm in a lot of pain.

items.pattern: an incurable illness / disease · incurable ↔ curable
items.meaning: an illness that doctors cannot cure
items.example: She was told she had an **incurable illness**, but she has lived well with it for twenty years.
more: Some diseases that were **incurable** fifty years ago can now be treated easily.
Living with an **incurable disease** taught him to enjoy every single day.
items.watchOut: «Невиліковний» — incurable, не unhealable. Heal — про рану, яка загоюється; cure — вилікувати хворобу.

items.pattern: minor / trivial ailments · an ailment is a formal word
items.meaning: small health problems that are not serious, like a sore throat or a headache
items.example: Pharmacists can help with **minor ailments**, so you don't always need to see a doctor.
more: Grandma has a home remedy for every **minor ailment**: honey, lemon and an early night.
Please don't call an ambulance for **trivial ailments** like a runny nose.
items.watchOut: Ailment — формальніше слово, ніж illness. «Легкі нездужання» — minor ailments, не light ailments.

items.pattern: a serious illness · be seriously ill
items.meaning: an illness that is dangerous or causes big problems
items.example: He had a **serious illness** as a teenager, but he's completely healthy now.
more: Meningitis is a **serious illness**, so call a doctor at once if you notice the symptoms.
My grandmother was **seriously ill** last winter, but she's much better now.
items.watchOut: «Тяжка хвороба» — a serious illness, не a heavy illness і не a hard illness. «Тяжко хворий» — seriously ill, не heavily ill.

items.pattern: a life-threatening illness / condition / injury · not life-threatening
items.meaning: so serious that it could kill you
items.example: A nut allergy can be **life-threatening**, so she always carries her medicine.
more: Luckily, his injuries aren't **life-threatening**, and he should be home in a week.
Call an ambulance straight away if you think the situation is **life-threatening**.
items.watchOut: «Небезпечний для життя» — life-threatening (через дефіс), не dangerous for life і не life-dangerous.

items.pattern: acutely / intensely / extremely painful
items.meaning: very painful, with sharp, strong pain
items.example: Breaking a toe is **intensely painful**, even though it's such a small bone.
more: The cut on my thumb was **acutely painful** every time I washed my hands.
Her shoulder became **intensely painful** whenever she lifted her arm.
items.watchOut: «Дуже болить» — it's very/extremely/intensely painful, не strongly painful. Painful — про те, що болить або завдає болю: a painful knee, a painful injection.

items.pattern: a dull ache / pain (in your back, tooth…)
items.meaning: a pain that is not strong or sharp but goes on for a long time
items.example: After the dentist, I had a **dull ache** in my jaw for the rest of the day.
more: I often get a **dull ache** in my lower back if I sit for too long.
I get a **dull ache** behind my eyes when I'm tired.
items.watchOut: «Тупий, ниючий біль» — a dull ache, не a stupid pain, не a blunt pain (blunt — тупий про ніж чи олівець) і не a deaf pain (калька з «глухий біль»).

items.pattern: prescribe (sb) tablets / medicine / antibiotics · a prescription
items.meaning: (of a doctor) say which medicine someone should take and give them a prescription for it
items.example: The doctor **prescribed some tablets** for my cough and told me to rest.
more: If the cream doesn't help, your GP can **prescribe** something stronger.
Take the antibiotics the doctor **prescribed** until you finish the whole packet.
items.watchOut: «Виписати ліки» — prescribe, не write out і не appoint medicine. Не плутай з describe (описати). «Приймати ліки» — take medicine/tablets, не drink tablets.

items.pattern: relieve / alleviate / ease the pain · pain relief
items.meaning: make pain less bad
items.example: A hot water bottle can help **relieve the pain** of a stomach ache.
more: The tablets **alleviated the pain** in my knee, but they made me sleepy.
Lying on the floor with my knees bent seems to **relieve the pain** in my back.
items.watchOut: «Полегшити біль» — relieve/ease the pain, не facilitate the pain і не take off the pain. Не плутай relieve /rɪˈliːv/ і release (відпустити). Alleviate /əˈliːvieɪt/ — формальніше.

items.pattern: be taken ill (suddenly) · was / were taken ill
items.meaning: suddenly become ill (mainly British)
items.example: Dad **was taken ill** at work and had to come home early.
more: One of the actors **was taken ill**, so the show was cancelled.
If you're **taken ill** abroad, your travel insurance should pay the hospital bills.
items.watchOut: Форма пасивна, але ніхто людину нікуди не «брав»: was taken ill — раптово захворів. «Йому стало погано» — he was taken ill або he felt ill, не he became bad (це «став поганим»).

items.pattern: a heavy / bad cold ↔ a slight cold
items.meaning: a bad cold, with a blocked nose, a cough and feeling very tired
items.example: I've got a **heavy cold**, so I'm staying in bed with tea and tissues.
more: She sounded awful on the phone: she had a **heavy cold** and could hardly speak.
A **heavy cold** can knock you out for a whole week.
items.watchOut: «Сильна застуда» — a heavy/bad cold, не a strong cold.

items.pattern: a slight cold ↔ a heavy cold
items.meaning: a mild cold that is not serious
items.example: It's only a **slight cold**, so I'm still going to work.
more: She had a **slight cold** on the day of the exam, but she did fine.
I've got a **slight cold**, nothing a hot drink won't fix.
items.watchOut: «Легка застуда» — a slight (або mild) cold, не an easy cold і не a weak cold.

items.pattern: have / wake up with a splitting headache
items.meaning: a very bad headache
items.example: After eight hours on a hot coach, I had a **splitting headache**.
more: I've had a **splitting headache** since lunch, so I'm going home early.
I woke up with a **splitting headache** after only three hours' sleep.
items.watchOut: «Сильно болить голова» — I've got a splitting/terrible headache, не a strong headache. Headache злічуване: a headache, з артиклем.

warmup.uk: Я захворів на грип і тиждень пролежав у ліжку.
warmup.q: I ___ the flu and spent a week in bed.
warmup.explain: Захворіти на грип — catch (або get) the flu. Застудитися — catch a cold.

warmup.uk: Лікар виписав мені таблетки від кашлю.
warmup.q: The doctor ___ me some tablets for my cough.
warmup.explain: Виписати ліки — prescribe. Appoint — призначити на посаду.

warmup.uk: Він отримав тяжкі травми в аварії.
warmup.q: He ___ serious injuries in the accident.
warmup.explain: Отримати травми — suffer або (формально) sustain injuries.

warmup.uk: На щастя, це була лише легка травма.
warmup.q: Luckily, it was only a ___ injury.
warmup.explain: Легка травма — a minor injury, тяжка — a serious injury.

warmup.uk: Коли я зламав руку, у мене був нестерпний біль.
warmup.q: When I broke my arm, I was in ___ pain.
warmup.explain: Сильний, нестерпний біль — excruciating/severe/terrible pain, не strong pain.
Terminally ill — хвороба невиліковна й смертельна. Urgently — терміново, це інше слово.

warmup.uk: Бабуся щодня плаває, щоб підтримувати форму.
warmup.q: Grandma swims every day to ___ fit.
warmup.explain: Підтримувати форму — keep fit (або stay fit).

A.q: My dad ___ from backache, so he can't carry heavy shopping.
A.explain: Suffer from — мати хронічну проблему. Sustain — про травми, contract — про інфекції.

A.q: He was ___ with diabetes at the age of forty.
A.explain: Be diagnosed with — отримати діагноз. Develop — без пасиву й без with: he developed diabetes.

A.q: The cyclist ___ minor injuries when he slipped on the ice.
A.explain: Sustain/suffer injuries — отримати травми. Contract і catch — про хвороби, не про травми.

B.q: I try to ___ some exercise every day, even if it's just a walk.
B.explain: Take (або do, get) exercise. Make exercise — калька.

B.q: She's tried lots of diets, but she never ___ to any of them for long.
B.explain: Stick to a diet / a plan — дотримуватися.

B.q: My grandad is eighty, but he's still in good ___.
B.explain: In good shape — у гарній формі. Figure — фігура, зовнішній вигляд.

C.q: My shoulder has been giving me a ___ ache since I started the new job.
C.explain: Тупий, ниючий біль — a dull ache. Blunt — тупий про ніж.

C.q: These tablets should help to ___ the pain.
C.explain: Полегшити біль — relieve (або ease, alleviate) the pain. Release — відпустити.

C.q: Our teacher was ___ ill during the school trip, so another teacher took over.
C.explain: Be taken ill — раптово захворіти. Можна й fell ill, але без was.

example.title: A healthy new year
example.uk:
У січні я вирішив підтримувати форму. Я почав займатися за програмою тренувань і пообіцяв собі, що не відступатиму від неї. Тричі на тиждень я інтенсивно тренувався й намагався збалансовано харчуватися.

Місяць усе йшло добре. Потім увесь мій офіс захворів на грип, а я одного ранку прокинувся із сильною застудою, і голова в мене розколювалася. Через тиждень я бігав у парку, послизнувся на льоду й підвернув ногу. Було дуже боляче, але лікарка сказала, що це лише легка травма. Вона виписала мені знеболювальне, щоб угамувати біль, і сказала, щоб я відпочивав.

Тепер березень. Я ще не в чудовій формі, але потроху до неї наближаюся.
example.en:
In January I decided to [[keep fit|b7]]. I started [[following a fitness programme|b5]] and promised myself I would [[stick to it|b6]]. I took [[vigorous exercise|b2]] three times a week and tried to [[eat a balanced diet|b3]].

For a month everything went well. Then my whole office [[caught the flu|a1]], and one morning I woke up with a [[heavy cold|c12]] and a [[splitting headache|c14]]. A week later I was running in the park, slipped on the ice and twisted my ankle. It was [[intensely painful|c7]], but the doctor said it was only a [[minor injury|a8]]. She [[prescribed painkillers|c9]] to [[relieve the pain|c10]] and told me to rest.

Now it's March. I'm not [[in great shape|b8]] yet, but I'm getting there.
